This pinpoints why state-name pigeonholing alone is too weak. Full proof: `research/C227_NATIVE_CERTIFICATE_SPLICE_LAW_2026-09-27.md`; no superlinear bound follows yet.

## C-228 - An artificial readout lower bound that evades splicing

Take a large structured family E of individually easy truth tables, then choose a random subfamily W of size R and let all non-W tables be rejecting. Counting q-state recurrence descriptions proves some W needs superpolynomial q, even though the seed-feature floor is linear. Choose W with no Hamming-neighbor pair; then every consistent accepting certificate fixes all N coordinates, and every safe splice can only identify an already accepted member. Thus global readout complexity need not arise from forbidden hybrid splicing. This is not the actual Gap-MCSP promise: the rejecting side includes easy tables. It teaches that O-151 must exploit the specific low/high circuit geometry, not generic certificate width or anchor abundance. Full construction: C-228 report.

## C-229 - Universal-circuit witness sharing loses global identity

For each low table, membership says there is one small circuit d matching every table coordinate. A separate verification chain per d is too large. Merging states across d allows the native positive grammar to combine support branches from different descriptions, which may create a hybrid not certified by any one circuit. Keeping d in the state preserves soundness but loses the desired compression. The exact missing object is a small semantic quotient of partial descriptions whose cross-products remain sound. This attempt supplies no lower bound; carriers might enforce consistency implicitly. See C-229 report.

## C-230 - Lupanov block shows the safe-cube width is essentially tight

A table-coordinate subcube with free addresses equal to an input-prefix block can lie entirely inside SIZE(s2): arbitrary labels on k remaining input bits have Lupanov circuits of size O(2^k/k), and the fixed prefix test costs O(n). Taking 2^k=Theta(s2 log s2) gives an all-non-high cube of dimension Theta(s2 log s2). Therefore the splice obstruction is exactly the maximum safe-cube dimension kappa_square, which is already Theta(s2 log s2); no large improvement comes from certificate width alone. Full proof and original-source link: C-230 report.

## Idea 353 - Small messages do not imply shared states (C-232)

For any Boolean f on N-bit inputs, its KW mismatch relation has only N coordinate outputs and an O(N)-bit deterministic protocol. By circuit counting, some such f has circuit size Omega(2^N/N); Sokolov's DAG/KW theorem makes its rect-DAG equally large up to constants. This proves that output count and communication do not generically control shared-DAG size. It does not transfer to Gap-MCSP. In C-75, Alice's circuit description makes the bit protocol cheap, but description-space and truth-table-space DAG sizes are identical. The direct universal separator still pays for `exists d forall k` and has size `N*2^(O(s1 log(n+s1)))`; its 2N mismatch rectangles are a cover, not a binary rectangle DAG. Continue O-152: prove an OPS-specific product-hull residual-separator charge above `N^(3+3epsilon)/log N`, or construct a near-linear full-promise DAG. Full proof and model table: `research/C232_SAME_ALPHABET_DAG_NONSHAREABILITY_CALIBRATION_2026-09-27.md`.

Calibration: do not let this route collapse to a one-anchor, universal, or fixed semi-filter family, since the recorded ceilings are `rho_w<=N-1`, `rho*=O(N)`, and `rho(H)=O(N log|H|)` in that fixed-family regime.

## Idea 354 â€” Minâ€“max activation ranks expose an event-driven closure

For each fusion rule i, assign rank `tau_i=1+max(L_i,R_i)`, where `L_i` and `R_i` are the minimum activation ranks among its two support families (a true seed has rank 0; no support means infinity). A Dijkstra-style worklist finalizes each rule once and scans every support arc once, so the closure is evaluable in `O(qN+(q+E)log q)=O(q^2 polylog q)` RAM time for successful OPS covers. This is a proved operational lemma and makes input-dependent rank ordering explicit; it does not yield an acyclic Boolean circuit because heap/memory access is dynamic.

Heathâ€“Kolesnikovâ€“Ostrovsky tri-state circuits can simulate the terminating RAM evaluator with `q^2 polylog q` gates, giving a separate, more expressive cyclic separator model. The direct activation network itself is an `O(q^2)` partial recognizer (YESâ†’1, NOâ†’Z); it is not a total Boolean separator. A lower bound above `N^(2+2epsilon+delta)` for these partial recognizers would force q superlinear, but no such bound is known. No standard rect-DAG or fusion lower bound follows; the active DAG compiler remains `O(q^3/log q)`. Next test only: an oblivious fan-in-two simulation of the worklist that preserves the quadratic area bound despite rank-reversing SCCs. Full proof and model boundary: `research/C233_MINMAX_ACTIVATION_RANK_AND_TRISTATE_RAM_BRIDGE_2026-09-27.md`. Source: Heath et al., [Tri-State Circuits: A Circuit Model that Captures RAM](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/095/).

C-235: Canonical endpoint law. Any consistent output-proof support defines a subcube interval `[ell,u]`; a splice intersects intervals, so its lower endpoint is the OR of positive supports and its upper endpoint the AND of negative-rail complements. Both endpoints must be in SIZE(s2), even if the cube dimension does not exceed `kappa_square`. The same law holds for multiple disjoint substitutions and all output-root side cross-pairs. This reframes the target as forcing a high ownership join/meet, but no such global forcing theorem is known; C-228 and the diagonal equality cover remain safe.

C-236: Disagreement-selector cap. For two repeated low anchors, each compatible splice chooses between the anchor bits on their disagreement set. The selector can be recovered from a low canonical endpoint and the two low anchors, so at most `|SIZE(s2)|=2^(o(N))` distinct masks occur even though a typical pair admits `2^(Omega(N))` possible masks. This makes the missing theorem precise: relate q-state grammar size to the structure/count of compatible masks, not to proof-tree count. The diagonal equality cover avoids the cap by restricting to prefix-constant masks. See C-236.

C-237: Typical disagreement sets still contain safe cubes of dimension Theta(s2 n), matching C-230. For beta<1/2 vary a subcube inside one differing suffix column; for beta>=1/2 vary arbitrary prefix functions on selected differing columns. Lupanov keeps all patches small. Thus random disagreement does not improve the local dimension barrier; next charge free-set geometry/description in the grammar.

C-238: Whole ranked witness skeletons mix globally. If two accepted anchors share the selected predecessor topology, take every E-side seed from one and every H-side seed from the other. A consistent union remains a finite accepting proof, so its whole cylinder is low. The crude count of possible skeletons was too large for anchor pigeonholing.

C-239 correction and refinement: state activation ranks alone do not determine side witnesses; a legal two-rule endpoint example has equal state ranks but different seed/predecessor choices on one side. Both side-support minima per state do determine one canonical skeleton. For fixed Q, its seed-signature vector has only 2q Boolean bits, so there are at most 2^(2q) canonical fibersâ€”sharper than the raw topology count, but not a count of all possible witness topologies and still too many at q>=N. The exact shared-state condition is conflict-or-cover: every context/replacement support pair either has opposite rails or jointly fixes all but kappa_square(s2) coordinates. One literal test per suffix address already distinguishes the repeated-anchor descriptions, so seed-profile pigeonholing cannot force collisions. The residual-circuit-description cover still lacks a compact update preserving one common description across all blocks. A monotone clique toy fails because its accepting cylinders are too wide. Full derivation and counterchecks: research/C239_CANONICAL_RANK_FIBERS_AND_NATIVE_SPLICE_OBLIGATION_2026-09-27.md.

C-241 shared-DAG continuation: the description input cannot lower standard rect-DAG size. For every onto truth-table map G:D->Y, lift a table-side graph through G and restrict a description-side graph to a section; this proves exact equality. A universal circuit does not eliminate the outer exists-d forall-k test. The direct minterm and dyadic restriction-profile DAGs remain exponential. The 2N mismatch rectangles give nondeterministic cover, not deterministic shared routing. Keep the exact chain rho_prom<=O(S_rect)<=O(rho_prom^3/log rho_prom) and require S_rect>N^(3+3epsilon)/logN for the generic transfer. No actual-promise lower bound follows. See research/C241_SHARED_DAG_DESCRIPTION_INVARIANCE_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 357 â€” Native fixed-order prefix-intersection cover

A concrete upper-bound attempt builds each realized low-table prefix as an intersection of matching high-side literal slices. One legal fusion pair extends a prefix by one coordinate. At length N-1, the two completions of a low table's prefix are both in SIZE(s2), since flipping one output costs O(n) and s1+O(n)<s2; therefore the high-side carrier is empty. The resulting cover has size at most sum_{t=2}^{N-1}|pi_t(SIZE(s1))|, hence at most N|SIZE(s1)|. It is not near-linear: uniform Theta(s1) shattering supplies 2^t distinct nonempty prefix carriers for t<=c s1. This rejects the fixed-order trie only; adaptive and non-prefix constructions remain open. See C-242.

## Idea 358 â€” High blockers coupled to safe splice intervals

The native closure has two exact views: an antichain grammar of minimal signed-literal supports, and for every high table a blocker side at each inactive state. A ranked proof for a low table follows the high blockers through low-active/high-inactive states and ends at a mismatching literal. Reusing a state additionally forces every consistent context/replacement join to have its entire Boolean interval inside SIZE(s2), including both the positive OR endpoint and the negative AND endpoint. The new target is to bound these safe interval joins jointly with blocker maps. The path alone is only pairwise and can be short; interval safety still has no q-charge. C-228 and C-234 remain hostile calibrations. See C-242.


## Idea 359 â€” State-zone factorisation as the global sharing object (C-244)

Cutting any accepting proof at an occurrence of state i gives a context support K; the removed subtree gives a proof support C. Conversely, any K and C that both match one table can be substituted to make an accepting proof. Hence Acc_Q(x)=OR_i(k_i(x) AND p_i(x)), where k_i ranges over all contexts with a hole at i and p_i over all finite proofs rooted at i. Each zone is safe, the q zones cover SIZE(s1), and every high table blocks at least one side of each zone.

This is a global exact form of the sharing hypothesis. It improves the bookkeeping object from a selected state collision to the entire context/proof cross-product at each state. The first aggregation still fails: a zone can be a union of exponentially many cylinders, and the grammar can have exponentially many derivations; there is no proved capacity bound in terms of q. Carrier volumes also do not add under correlated intersections. Next seek a joint generation/entropy theorem for (K_i,P_i) that uses actual SIZE geometry, while continuing the full-promise near-linear cover search. C-228 and C-234 are hostile checks. Full proof and exact limits: research/C244_STATE_ZONE_FACTORISATION_AND_GLOBAL_READOUT_2026-09-27.md.

C-243 companion fact: every high table extending a proof support rooted at i lies in T_i, yielding |T_i| >= 2^(N-|dom(C)|)-M2 and a packing bound for disjoint high cylinder portions. This remains state-local and has no additive q-charge; see research/C243_CARRIER_VOLUME_AND_CERTIFICATE_PACKING_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 360 â€” One-hole differentiation of the antichain proof grammar (C-245)

A proof state is an antichain-semiring expression: alternatives add by Min, and the two rule sides multiply by compatible support union. Mark one occurrence of state i as a hole. At an AND/product, the hole propagates through either side while the other side remains an ordinary proof. This gives an exact joint grammar for P_i and K_i, rather than treating contexts as arbitrary sets.

A context and replacement proof that match the same input can be represented with context height at most 2q: delete repeated states along the path to the hole and use rank-minimal proofs on the side branches. The q^2 context-family labels do not bound the antichain sizes, so this is a formalization tool, not a lower bound. The next missing theorem is a q-bounded invariant for the generated context/proof join tensor that forces either a high endpoint or excessive state cost. Full proof and caveats: research/C245_MARKED_ANTICHAIN_GRAMMAR_FOR_CONTEXTS_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 361 â€” Certificate count cannot pay for state sharing (C-246)

For the C-234 repeated family, a safe support cylinder with at most kappa free table coordinates can match at most 2^(kappa/r) diagonal anchors: if any repeated copy of suffix u is fixed, it fixes g(u). Since kappa/r=o(s2), exponentially many certificates are needed to cover all repeated anchors.

But a q-state grammar has at most q*2^q*(2N+q)^(2q) ranked witness-DAG certificates. At q=Theta(N), this is exp(O(N logN)), far above exp(Theta(s2)), so certificate counting cannot improve the linear floor. Retire raw support cardinality; target the geometry of which context/proof pairs are compatible and what endpoints their joins produce. Full audit: research/C246_REPEATED_BLOCK_CERTIFICATE_CAP_AND_COUNTING_FAILURE_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 362 â€” Multi-hole splice partition function (C-247)

For pairwise disjoint marked occurrences in an accepting proof, substitute all chosen rooted proofs simultaneously. Every globally consistent support union gives an accepted cylinder. If replacement choices have associated anchor completions with distinct projections on private sets D_j, disjoint from every other slot and the outside context, then distinct tuples yield distinct tables, so product_j |A_j|<=|SIZE(s2)|.

C-234 block isolation violates this budget with 2^N hybrids and is impossible in a sound closure. The linear-size diagonal equality cover evades the premise by fingerprinting g in every context. The unresolved object is the consistency hypergraph of replacement tuples: prove a small grammar must expose many compatible, independent slots, or pay superlinear state cost to suppress them. Entropy alone cannot exceed N. Full derivation: research/C247_MULTIHole_SPLICE_ENTROPY_BUDGET_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 363 â€” Native blocker rectangles and recursive cross-pair routing (C-248)

For each state i, pair every low table activating i with every high table on which i is inactive. This full rectangle R_i is forced by state reuse. A high-blocked side and a low-side witness route every pair either to a signed mismatch rectangle or to a predecessor rectangle; low activation rank guarantees termination. This gives the exact global product-hull law to study for O-153.

The attempt to use rectangle area/count immediately fails: any disjoint low/high promise has a 2N signed-mismatch rectangle cover. A sharper counterexample is Y=all nonconstant strings and Z={0^N,1^N}: one rule E={1^N}, H={0^N} accepts exactly Y, so R_1=YÃ—Z has exponential area at q=1. Each pair uses its own coordinate mismatch; the rectangle cross-product does not splice table pieces. The resource to charge is the single shared recursive two-sided routing system, not its rectangle leaves or state areas.

Also, q fixed-point rounds yield a monotone separator extension of at most 3qÂ²+1 unbounded-fan-in gates when wires are free. Incidences are O(qÂ²(N+q)), cubic near q=N, so this compiler does not improve the ordinary circuit transfer. No bound for the actual promise follows. See research/C248_BLOCKER_RECTANGLES_AND_MONOTONE_EXTENSION_COMPILER_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 364 â€” Bi-blocked output roots (C-249)

Every signed half-cube contains a high table in the OPS regime. At any accepted low input, choose the minimum-rank active empty-carrier root. An empty endpoint cannot witness a nonempty seed slice; a predecessor fitting inside it would be another empty root active earlier. So the useful root has two nonempty disjoint endpoints. Choosing z_EâˆˆE_i and z_HâˆˆH_i gives fixed high blockers for the opposite sides.

C-240 then limits direct root seeds to one complementary literal selector or a seedless side, and each proof must escape to a predecessor. This normalizes the first step of the proof DAG, but does not charge q: the same predecessor row set can serve many low anchors. The next target is to aggregate these fixed-witness escapes with the context/proof splice relation. See research/C249_BIBLOCKED_OUTPUT_ROOT_NORMAL_FORM_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 366 â€” Root escape support dichotomy (C-251)

At a normalized empty output root, inspect a low anchor's selected proof. If a direct seed matches, the other side must use a predecessor, whose support is half-safe by C-250. If no direct seed matches, both sides use predecessors; their support union is consistent, and every completion preserves the empty-root proof, so the whole union cylinder is low. Every accepted low therefore has either a one-sided half-safe escape support or a two-sided wholly-low paired support, including seedless roots. On repeated-block anchors either signature type covers at most 2^((kappa+1)/r) anchors.

This closes the local support-capacity gap but not the q-charge. Paired proof-DAG counts square the old upper bound only up to constants, leaving exp(O(q log(N+q))) descriptions. The next theorem must charge state reuse through cross-root support incidence/compatibility, or construct a near-linear full-promise cover. No lower bound follows from per-signature capacity. Full proof and failure: research/C251_ROOT_ESCAPE_SUPPORT_DICHOTOMY_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 367 â€” Quotient root escapes to a state-conflict graph (C-252)

For each empty output root i, every pair of active predecessor states (j\in P_i,k\in R_i) is forbidden on high tables: C-243 would put a high table in both disjoint endpoints. A matching direct seed on one side plus an active opposite predecessor is likewise forbidden. Conversely every accepted low triggers one of these patterns. Collapsing over roots yields at most q^2 directed state conflicts and at most 2qN state/literal incidences, giving a depth-two readout with at most q^2+2qN terms.

This quotients exponentially many certificate supports into state fibres and gives a concise representation of O-153 cross-root interaction. In the OPS regime q=Omega(N), the ordinary circuit transfer remains O(q^2), matching C-248, and graph independence alone does not bound the number of high tables sharing a profile. Next target: a fibre-geometry/VC or closure invariant linking the q-state activation map to the actual circuit-complexity promise, or a near-linear cover. Graph size and edge count alone are not lower bounds. Full theorem and failed amplification: research/C252_STATE_CONFLICT_GRAPH_READOUT_2026-09-27.md.


## Idea 365 â€” Half-safe escape supports at seedful roots (C-250)

At a minimum-rank output root with a direct seed literal (k,b), a low anchor matching that literal cannot exit through an opposite-side seed. It must use a predecessor. The high half-cube inside the seed side is excluded from the opposite endpoint and hence from the predecessor carrier. C-243 then says every high completion of an escape support avoids bit b, so that half of the support cylinder is all low. This forces at most ceil(log2|SIZE(s2)|)+1 free coordinates.

On repeated-block anchors this gives a per-support capacity of 2^((kappa+1)/r), recovering the certificate-capacity phenomenon for seedful branches. Taking the result to its limit still fails at certificate-to-state counting: q states permit exp(O(q log(N+q))) ranked witness-DAG descriptions, which is too many at the linear scale. Seedless roots still need the two-sided C-242/C-247 join analysis. Next seek a grammar-wide reuse charge, not a stronger local width bound. Full derivation: research/C250_ONE_SIDED_SAFE_ESCAPE_CYLINDERS_2026-09-27.md.

## Idea 368 ? Conflict-profile fibres are marker subcubes (C-253)

For any exact activation profile sigma, a conflict edge makes its whole fibre low. If sigma is conflict-free, its active states carry a marker set B_sigma: every low table in that fibre matches a marker, whereas every high table avoids all markers. Thus the high fibre lies in a subcube fixing r_sigma coordinates and has size at most 2^(N-r_sigma). Summing over the I independent profiles actually represented on U gives r_min<=log2(I)+o(1)<=q+o(1).

The bound may be witnessed by a profile with no low members; graph entropy alone does not link low-output states to the profiles covering U. Two-coordinate high-side shattering is compatible with one high profile that has no markers. The next test is a closure-specific coupling under coordinate flips or partial supports. No lower bound follows from this count. Full proof and failure: research/C253_CONFLICT_PROFILE_FIBRE_SUBCUBES_2026-09-27.md.

## Idea 369 ? Hazard boundaries on the partial-support lattice (C-254)

Extend state activation from complete tables to partial supports C by asking whether a finite proof has all its leaves in C. If the resulting profile triggers a conflict edge or active-state/seed incidence, every completion activates an empty output root and is low. So every low table's first hazardous prefix in every coordinate order must fix at least N-log2|SIZE(s2)| bits.

Selected-witness correction: a readout-term witness has at most q distinct state labels and at most two seed leaves per state, plus one marker, so its hazardous support has width <=2q+1. The cylinder bound gives q >= (N-log2|SIZE(s2)|-1)/2, only a linear floor below the known N-o(N) bound. The unresolved step is overlap-safe aggregation of such witness DAGs across low anchors, not chain event counting. See corrected C-254.


## Idea 371 â€” Residual-hull state charge for the C-75 mismatch DAG (C-255)

A shared state v owns a full product rectangle A_v x B_v. If K_v is its descendant output-coordinate set, safety requires disjoint projections pi_Kv(A_v) and pi_Kv(B_v). When histories merge, the suffix sees the product hull of the unions, not the separate incoming rectangles. Search for a residual signature/potential that decreases under child routing and can be globally charged without counting the same excluded high columns at many states. C-80/C-160/C-232 are hostile checks. Local density and anchor counts fail. Current compiler threshold: S_rect>N^(3+3epsilon)/log N to force rho>N^(1+epsilon); a near-linear adaptive DAG would falsify that route. No candidate potential proved. See research/C255_SHARED_DAG_ROUTE_RESTART_2026-09-27.md.

## Idea 372 â€” Bottleneck counting for mismatch width and BPHP source transfer (C-255)

Beameâ€“Whitmeyer prove a `2^(Omega(m^(1/4)))` triangle-DAG lower bound for bit-pigeonhole search using a node bottleneck map and per-node capacity lemma. At `m=K(log N)^4`, its quantitative lower bound can clear our cubic/log transfer threshold. A common hard-translate lemma now handles the image hurdle: because `|SIZE(s1)||SIZE(s2)|=2^o(N)`, some mask `r` lies outside `SIZE(s1) xor SIZE(s2)`, so every low base codeword `u` maps to a high table `u xor r`. The remaining hurdle is exact answer soundness: coordinate mismatches become diagonal or off-diagonal bit rectangles, and each signed rectangle must be valid for a fixed source output label. No BPHP low code with this property is known. The direct mismatch bottleneck width `lambda_v(w)` also still needs a per-node capacity bound. No transfer or C-75 lower bound is proved. See C-255 and the primary paper at https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol334-icalp2025/html/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.21/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.21.html.
### Idea 373 â€” Common-translate answer-code reconstruction obstruction (C-256)

Static output-label decoding can leak enough structure to reconstruct the supposedly hard mask. For a two-wise-rich hard KW partition with 0,e_i on one side and 1^M on the other, every active C-75 coordinate must encode one source bit with the same phase on both parties. The active-coordinate indicator is OR_i(u_0 xor u_ei), and r=v_1 xor u_0 xor active; this costs O(Ms1). The full-domain BPHP source is also blocked: both signed labels at an active target coordinate would make the Alice domain the union of two fixed collision-equality sets, which cannot cover it. These are reduction-interface no-go results, not target lower bounds. Next test whether terminal-specific decoding has a small enough binary-DAG refinement cost; otherwise focus on direct bottleneck capacity or an actual C-75 DAG construction. See C-256.

### Idea 374 â€” Parity-code splicing lock (C-257)

For the artificial promise Y=even-parity strings and U=odd-parity strings, every proper partial assignment extends to a high string. Nonetheless an explicit native closure with `4N-4` pairs accepts all even anchors: propagate prefix-parity carriers by intersecting with the next matching literal slice, then use the final parity contradiction. Every consistent output proof fixes all N bits, and every consistent context/subproof splice therefore names an even string. This defeats any generic sharing-to-high theorem based only on high-side shattering, full certificate width, and anchor abundance. The actual theorem must exploit that low circuits need one shared short description and that mixed blocks may exceed its description budget. This toy is not Gap-MCSP and yields no superlinear bound. Full proof: `research/C257_PARITY_CODE_SPLICE_LOCKING_CALIBRATION_2026-09-27.md`.

### Idea 375 - Native equality-fingerprint subcover (C-258)

If low anchors are constant on d blocks of r truth-table coordinates, an explicit native list with `2N+2d-1` pairs checks each block's two constant patterns and intersects the block carriers. This works against the actual high set `U=complement SIZE(s2)` whenever the repeated family lies in `SIZE(s1)`. It recovers the diagonal equality escape from C-234 without passing through a generic separator-to-fusion compiler. It covers only that structured subfamily; extending it to all small circuits would require a compact family of fingerprints, while a lower bound must rule out other endpoint geometries. See `research/C258_REPEATED_BLOCK_NATIVE_COVER_2026-09-27.md`.

### Idea 376 - Product-code closure bound (C-258)

The repeated-block construction extends to any Cartesian product of local codebooks `A_j` on coordinate blocks `B_j`. If the product family is disjoint from U and every literal slice of U is nonempty, prefix chains for each local word, one existential merge per block, and a final block intersection give a native cover with `q<=sum_j |A_j||B_j|+2d-1`. The bound shows exactly when local pattern libraries remain cheap; it suggests upper-bound work should search for a small product-code cover of the full low-circuit class. No such cover is known, and the theorem does not lower-bound q for Gap-MCSP. See C-258.

## C-257 / C-258 splice-and-fingerprint graph

Odd-parity high set --prefix-parity proof states--> `4N-4`-rule even/odd cover (C-257)
  --high side extends every proper partial assignment--> every consistent output support fixes all N bits
  --finite context/proof substitution--> every consistent splice is even

Repeated-block family `Rep_{d,r} subseteq SIZE(s1)` --block-prefix carriers--> merge two block values --intersect across d blocks--> empty carrier since `U intersect Rep=empty` (C-258)
  --direct native list--> `q=2N+2d-1` for this subfamily against the actual high set

Thus a compact semantic fingerprint can protect extensive state reuse even on the actual high side. Missing edge: cover all `SIZE(s1)` with a near-linear collection of such regions, or prove the full class forces superlinear q despite every alternative fingerprint. Neither toy construction changes the full-promise bound.

### Idea 377 - The cofactor/splice threshold is Theta(n) (C-259)

A prefix mux of t size-s1 cofactors has size `t s1+O(t)`. Since the OPS ratio is `s2/s1=cn`, every simple hybrid using up to a small constant times n low pieces remains in SIZE(s2). Conversely, C-247's private-slot theorem says t independent replacement slots, each with `2^(Theta(s2))` choices, exceed the total size-s2 class only once t is above `C n`. This explains why one-hole or constant-hole splicing cannot yield the desired contradiction. The missing link is still to force `Omega(n)` such independent slots (or a hard selector) from a q-state grammar and charge their suppression. See C-259 and C-116.

### Idea 378 - Pair proof joins with their dual blockers (C-260)

Every native state has a minimal present-feature certificate antichain and a minimal absent-feature blocker antichain, with the latter exactly the transversal family of the former. Cutting at a shared state gives the exact output-certificate convolution `K_i join P_i`; every compatible join is hit by every output blocker. Pigeonholing also forces an internal state to serve at least `2^d/q` anchors on a repeated-block subfamily with `d log d=O(s1)`, but C-258 shows equality fingerprints keep that reuse safe at O(N) cost. The global object to charge is the incidence geometry of context/replacement joins against the shared blocker grammar. The current law only guarantees nonempty intersection, so it yields no q bound. Seek a q-sensitive incidence multiplicity or transversal-slack theorem. See C-260.

### Idea 379 â€” Spread matching survives cyclic AND states (C-261)

Use v-vertex bipartite matching against graphs with no v/4-matching. Rao's current spread-matching lower bound is exp(Omega(sqrt(v))) for ordinary monotone circuits. A q-state least-fixed-point grammar stabilizes by round q; unrolling q rounds into binary monotone gates costs O(q^2(v^2+q)). Therefore CycAnd on this promise is still exp(Omega(sqrt(v))). This is source-side only but resolves the cycle-model audit. Full proof: research/C261_MATCHING_CYCLIC_LOWEXT_AND_GLOBAL_ROUTE_AUDIT_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 380 â€” Parameterize LowExt at logarithmic-square matching size (C-262)

Take v=A(ln N)^2. The cyclic source hardness becomes N^(c sqrt(A)); source input length is Theta(log^4 N), and poly(v) completion circuits fit s1=N^beta/(c0 log N) for every fixed beta. If map AND cost a<=N^eta, choose c sqrt(A)>max(1+epsilon,eta) with margin. The parameter obstacle is gone conditional on a map; the remaining challenge is a monotone signed-partial-table encoding with a high completion on NO inputs. See C-262.

### Idea 381 â€” LowExt needs global witness validity (C-263)

A direct sparse code makes table 1s name matching edges and gives 0-rails universally. It admits the all-zero low table even on NO graphs. Complementing it admits the all-one table. Fixing one baseline coordinate still leaves easy one-bit perturbations. The reduction must constrain every low completion to behave like a valid witness without using nonmonotone graph-absence tests. Search block summaries of absent rails or a code family with a global completion-validity mechanism; the naive incidence template is closed.

### Idea 382 â€” Compatibility matrices need grammar cost (C-264)

Define Comp_i(w,w') when a context matching w and a proof for w' at i have a consistent union. Pair the compatible joins with output blockers. C-258 demonstrates that equality fingerprints can restrict this matrix cheaply with q=O(N), so row counts, pair counts, and blocker hits cannot be the invariant. Charge the representation of many description-dependent compatibility relations for the full low-circuit class.

### Idea 383 â€” Independent cofactor recursion exceeds the soundness budget (C-265)

A multilevel product cover permits R independent size-s1 leaf circuits and can accept tables of mux size about R s1. Soundness caps R at O(log N); making each leaf arbitrary requires R=N^(1-beta+o(1)). Retire the naive product recursion. Any viable full-promise near-linear cover must preserve a global description across blocks or introduce a coherence-preserving quotient.

### Idea 384 - Cyclic spread-matching proof boundary (C-266)

Rao's spread matching theorem does apply to the native cyclic AND measure, but by a concrete compiler: solve the free union equations as ORs of generators and q AND states, then unroll the inflationary q-state update for q rounds. This costs O(q^2(v^2+q)) fan-in-two monotone gates. Directly recycling Rao's approximation proof around a cycle is unjustified because gate approximants require a topological induction and feedback can reintroduce prior error. The compiler repairs this with polynomial loss. It proves a source lower bound only; no LowExt map follows.

### Idea 385 - Exact logarithmic-square source scale, map still absent (C-267)

For v=A(log N)^2, matching source hardness is N^(c' sqrt(A)-o(1)). A map of AND cost at most N^eta gives q>N^(1+epsilon) if c' sqrt(A)>max(1+epsilon,eta) by a fixed margin. Every poly(v) YES completion fits s1 for each fixed beta>0. This is the exact parameter window. The open object is a monotone signed-rail map satisfying both low YES completion and high NO completion.

### Idea 386 - Partial-MCSP ETH hardness is not LowExt transfer (C-268)

Ilango's reduction encodes permutation choices through optimal monotone read-once formulas on a full truth-table partial function. It is algorithmic ETH-hardness, not a source-monotone map with a charged AND count, and it gives no high unrestricted-circuit completion on NO inputs. Borrow only the description-synchronization motif; verify all three transfer obligations independently.

### Idea 387 - Fully pinned hard baseline cannot be easy to patch (C-269)

If a NO image fully pins a high z and a YES low witness w_M differs from z on an easily computed coordinate mask D_M, then z=w_M XOR 1_{D_M}. When the mask costs at most s2-s1-O(1), this contradicts z being high. This closes structured edge-block patch masks on a common full baseline, not partial NO images with hidden unpinned bits.

### Idea 388 - Global compatibility tensor calibrated, not charged (C-270)

The statewise context/proof relation plus output blockers captures all safe joins, but no measure on its row/column counts forces superlinear states. C-258's equality fingerprint synchronizes an exponential repeated-block family using 2N+2d-1 pairs. Need a full-SIZE(s1) incompatibility property that cannot be handled by such a coordinate fingerprint, then a grammar-cost lower bound. The expander-overlap construction is a candidate to formulate, not a result.

### Idea 389 - BPHP sink refinement needs hole localization and a DAG, not a cover

A generic source sink rectangle can contain all hole values for one colliding pigeon pair. Refining it into fixed-clause answer rectangles takes 2^n0 distinct labels; a rectangle cover alone is not a binary rect-DAG because arbitrary rectangle unions are not rectangles. At n0=K log^4 N, generic enumeration overwhelms the 2^(Omega(n0^(1/4))) source lower bound. Only a proved property of actual pulled-back sinks that localizes hole values can rescue the route.

### Idea 390 - Worklist event count does not yet give an ordinary circuit

The sequential least-fixed-point algorithm activates each state once and scans each support incidence once, but an oblivious circuit must route the input-dependent queue and update side flags. Synchronous unrolling costs O(qE); a near-E sorting/routing compiler is unproved. Any proposal must count dynamic selection and writes explicitly.

### Idea 391 - Near-linear universal-circuit quotient keeps hitting description coherence (C-271)

Explicitly enumerate descriptions and compare all N table coordinates: `N*2^{O(s1 log(s1+n))}` AND cost. Merge by block restrictions: different blocks may choose different circuits, producing a hybrid outside the soundness budget. Recursively split into independent cofactors: only O(log N) pieces remain sound, while a trivial base needs `N^(1-beta+o(1))`. Index states by exact subfunction: the shattered sparse-indicator family already gives superpolynomially many. All three implementations fail; no general semantic-quotient obstruction is proved. See research/C271_NEAR_LINEAR_UNIVERSAL_CIRCUIT_QUOTIENT_AUDIT_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 392 - Expander-copy code creates many high hybrids, but one graph is cheap to synchronize (C-272)

Take V=Theta(s2) vertices, b=logV, and a strongly explicit constant-degree expander. Every C:{0,1}^b->{0,1} has Lupanov size O(V/b)<=s1 with a small constant. On r=Theta(logN) copies of each directed edge, write the low table value C(u) XOR C(v). This yields E=Theta(s2 logN) overlapping local views. Since log|SIZE(s2)|=O(s2 logN), choosing the copy factor large makes 2^E independent edge-copy hybrids mostly high. Expansion makes vertex-label changes affect many views. However one graph's parity/cut consistency can be checked in O(E), and E=o(N) at this scale; no grammar forces those independent replacements. Route B needs many incompatible wirings plus a global q-charge. See C-272.

### Idea 393 - Example lists give the wrong rail order for LowExt (C-273)

The natural specified-rail vector P for a consistent example list lies below any fitting code e(w), but C-125 needs e(w)<=phi(YES). Reversing the order with an upper-completion vector makes both rails present at unspecified coordinates, so that vector cannot lie below any one-hot NO high code. The NO-side high completion itself is easy: when m=poly(logN) positions are fixed in an N-entry table, 2^(N-m) completions outnumber SIZE(s2)=2^{o(N)}. C-125 allows low completions on NO inputs too. The remaining challenge is one source-monotone, low-AND-cost map that realizes the asymmetric orders. The recent learning paper supplies neither that map nor an unconditional source hardness theorem. See research/C273_MONOTONE_EXAMPLE_HARDNESS_TO_LOWEXT_AUDIT_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 394 - Patchable conflict support pays the source lower bound (C-274)

For any C-125 map on an upward-closed YES set, low witnesses across YES inputs agree outside the coordinates conflicted somewhere on a YES: join two inputs and monotonicity activates both rails wherever their witness bits differ. If the union S of conflict coordinates is small enough, a monotone AND of the common witness rails outside S separates YES from NO, because a NO high completion agreeing there would be a point-minterm patch of a low table. Formally, if s1+K logN(|S|+1)<=s2 then CycAnd(f)<=a+N-|S|-1, where a is the map's AND cost. A useful matching transfer must therefore use Omega((s2-s1)/logN)=Omega(N^beta/logN) globally conflicted coordinates. This strengthens the logN support threshold in C-127, but does not rule out broad rare conflicts or change q. See research/C274_CONFLICT_SUPPORT_PATCHING_OBSTRUCTION_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 395 - LowExt matching map needs Omega(s2) global conflict support (C-275/C-276)

Shared block decoding improves arbitrary k-coordinate patching from O(k logN) to O(k logN/log k). For `s1=N^beta/(c0 logN)` and `s2=N^beta`, every conflict union of size at most `c_beta s2` remains patchable into a low circuit. Thus a map capable of transferring Rao's cyclic matching lower bound past `N^(1+epsilon)` must have more than `c_beta s2` globally conflicted truth-table positions and map AND-cost below `L(v)-N^(1+epsilon)`, where `v=A(log N)^2`. This does not bound simultaneous conflicts or provide the map. Source and parameter audit: research/C276_ROUTE_A_PARAMETER_AND_CYCLIC_SOURCE_AUDIT_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 396 - Hall cuts require AND interactions in a matching LowExt map (C-277)

If each output rail is only an OR of graph-edge bits, consistency on one- and two-edge NO graphs forces one fixed polarity per truth-table coordinate. Every YES then carries the same low table, so the map induces an N-clause monotone CNF for matching threshold. For every vertex cover W of size v/4-1, the graph G_W of all edges incident to W is NO. Hall's theorem bounds how many such G_W one blocker clause can reject by 2^(v/2-1), while the number of W is 2^(H_2(1/4)v-o(v)); therefore the CNF needs 2^(0.311...v-o(v)) clauses. Since v=A(log N)^2, this exceeds N. Lesson: an OR-only witness encoding cannot work; AND interactions must create varying low codes while preserving NO consistency. This does not bound maps with positive AND-cost. See research/C277_HALL_CUT_OBSTRUCTION_TO_OR_ONLY_LOWEXT_MAP_2026-09-27.md.


### Idea 397 - A fixed NO scaffold cannot hide a witness-union map (C-278)

Suppose NO inputs all map to a fixed partial rail vector P and YES inputs only add witness-dependent rails psi. Since P lies below a high code, it contains no low code. A YES low code must therefore use at least one rail outside P, while NO inputs activate no such rails. ORing all excess output rails computes the source using the map's same AND gates, so `a>=CycAnd(f)`. This covers empty-NO images and any fixed high/partial baseline with witness rails added only on YES. It does not cover input-dependent NO decoys. Thus a useful LowExt transfer must make the NO-side partial assignment vary with the source input while keeping it high-completable and low-code-free. See research/C278_FIXED_NO_BASELINE_WITNESS_MAP_AND_EXTRACTION_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 398 - Rank-state palettes meet LowExt but expose a short decoder (C-279)

For two disjoint matching instances, threshold predicates `R_t=[nu(G1)>=t AND nu(G2)>=m+1-t]` activate once at the NO boundary `nu1+nu2=m+1` and at least twice on YES `nu1+nu2>=m+2`. Assign each t a high table whose 1-set is a disjoint address class. One boundary state gives a complete high NO code; two adjacent states give both rails needed for the low zero table. Counting supplies all high class indicators at `m=Theta(log^2 N)`. The map is valid, but the source is recovered by `OR_t(R_t AND R_(t+1))`; one output coordinate per class exposes each R_t. Hence its map cost is at least the source CycAnd complexity minus O(m), leaving only an O(log^2 N) transfer gap. Lesson: varying NO codes is insufficient if their activation profile has a short decoder. Seek many witness-indexed profiles with no cheap pairwise decoder. Full proof: research/C279_RANK_CODE_LOWEXT_MAP_AND_DECODER_COST_2026-09-27.md.
### Idea 399 - Owner masks are the global consistency witness for a splice (C-281)

Cut an accepting native derivation at a shared state into a context support K and replacement support P. If K matches low table w and P matches low table w', then compatibility gives a canonical owner mask `mu=Var(P)\Var(K)`: the hybrid takes w' on coordinates mentioned only by P and w elsewhere. It completes the joined support, so it must be in SIZE(s2). For fixed w,w', distinct mask restrictions on their disagreement set give distinct low hybrids. The project target is now a q-dependent bound on these state-indexed compatible mask products, not another certificate-width bound. Parity and repeated-block equality are mandatory safe-splice tests. No q improvement follows yet; the actual bound remains N-o(N). See research/C281_NATIVE_CYLINDER_GRAMMAR_AND_OWNER_MASK_FRONTIER_2026-09-27.md.

### Idea 400 - Bottom-NO collision attempt corrected by compatible completions (C-283)

C-282 incorrectly inferred a two-rail collision at a coordinate where the bottom partial image may be blank. For `P=phi(0)` with d holes and K compatible low tables, collisions on pinned coordinates plus tests on the hole bits give `CycAnd(f)<=a+(N-d)+K max(d-1,0)`. A nonempty K plus a high bottom completion forces `d=Omega_beta(s2)` by sparse-support interpolation. This is not sufficient: C-279 has empty P and a large K but exposes a short source decoder. The exact C-125 interface remains open. See C-283.

### Idea 401 - Scale matching source dimension polynomially, then attack only the map (C-284)

For `v=N^delta`, choose `0<delta<min(beta,1-beta)`. Matching-incidence witness tables cost `O(v logN/logv)=O(v/delta)<=s1`; Rao's cyclic lower bound grows as `exp(Omega(N^(delta/2)))`; and counting permits `N^delta` balanced address classes all to be high. This removes source-size arithmetic as a bottleneck but leaves the actual hard part: monotone rail-map validity, high NO completions, and no short decoder. Scaling the C-279 rank palette still fails. See C-284.

### Idea 402 - Expander overlap of raw projections collapses to coordinate classes (C-285)

Let each local view be a restriction to S_v?[N]. A compatible tuple of views agrees on every shared coordinate and therefore glues to one unique assignment on the union of the S_v. For each coordinate, a spanning tree over its occurrences generates every equality constraint; adding expander edges does not create new degrees of freedom. Thus edge count/expansion is not a native synchronization cost. Any surviving overlap construction must use nonprojection relations and prove that the closure pays for enforcing them. This kills only the raw-projection proposal; it gives no q bound or full cover. See C-285.

### Idea 403 - Shared Rao approximation has no output multiplier, but only directionally (C-286)

Rao's gatewise matching-DNF construction bounds missed true rails on YES and invented rails on NO. OR gates propagate these events without adding errors; each distinct AND node contributes once even if many output rails reuse it. The requested full two-sided disagreement statement is unsupported, but the directional sandwich suffices for the proof. See C-286.

For `v` source vertices, `theta_M=Theta(v^-1/2)+O(logN/v)`. At `v=Theta(log^2N)`, the expected canonical disagreement radius is `Theta(N/logN)`, far beyond `N^beta`. Raising `v` to meet patchability conflicts with fitting direct matching-indicator witness tables into `SIZE(s1)` for small beta. The canonical-table argument excludes C-125 maps below `A_map=L0/4`, after repairing the promise to `k=2ell>ell`. ### Idea 406 - ODDFACTOR span witnesses need coherent NO decoys (C-288)

ODDFACTOR has a GF(2) span program of size linear in its edge variables, while monotone decision needs `m^(Omega(logm))`. A sparse solution is a low candidate table, but solution-use rail predicates vanish on all NO inputs; ORing them recovers the source with the same AND budget. ### Idea 407 - [Crosswalk] Robust completion cylinders are already in C-244 (C-289)

The proof-term view is a direct DNF expansion of C-244's state-zone factorization. C-230 already pins the maximum safe-cube dimension at `Theta_beta(N^beta logN)` via Lupanov synthesis and counting. C-289 only makes explicit that such a cylinder can exceed the whole low class because of medium completions. Keep the active effort on C-244's low-mass/readout charge and O-168; this is not a new branch.

### Idea 408 - ODDFACTOR now has an exponential source gap, but dual sidecars are visible shortcuts (C-291)

Cavalar et al. give an exponential monotone circuit lower bound for ODDFACTOR while its monotone GF(2) span program remains linear. Cyclic unrolling preserves an exponential-in-a-power-of-v source lower bound. Taking `v=(log N)^K` for large enough fixed K makes this exceed all polynomial encoder costs, and an odd-factor edge-set witness is still a polylog-size table. This removes source hardness and witness size as the bottlenecks; C-125 map validity remains the bottleneck.

The tempting repair â€œput a dual witness in extra input bitsâ€ fails if yes instances set all those rails and no instances set a consistent one-hot code. `AND` of all auxiliary rails distinguishes those promises cheaply, even if the selected no code is a high-complexity table. Learning: never count a high completion as a hard decoy until checking whether the source input exposes an easy monotone selector for which side supplied it. The decoy must be generated from the hard graph or the augmented promise needs its own lower bound. See `research/C291_ODDFACTOR_EXPONENTIAL_SOURCE_AND_WITNESS_SIDECAR_NO_GO_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 409 - Opposite ODDFACTOR rails need YES certificate unions (C-292)

An edge set is contained in an odd-cut NO graph iff it has an odd-order connected component. Hence any positive certificate for a table bit's 0 rail, united with any positive certificate for its 1 rail, must be ODDFACTOR-YES and contain an odd-factor subgraph. This turns NO consistency into a concrete span-witness condition. It also sharpens the issue with a linear GF(2) span program: the selected edge support is a candidate table's 1-set, but a total one-hot code needs monotone evidence for its omitted edges too. OR-only maps cannot supply the complementary certificate pairs; positive-AND sharing must build them globally without an easy NO-side shortcut. This is a structural target, not a CohEnc lower bound. See `research/C292_ODDFACTOR_CERTIFICATE_COMPLEMENTARITY_AND_OR_ONLY_FILTER_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 410 - Every ODDFACTOR bit with two possible polarities costs width (C-293)

With `a` fan-in-two AND gates, any nonzero monotone output rail has some positive certificate using at most `a+1` edge variables; extract a connected proof DAG and count its binary AND branching. C-292 requires a pair of opposite-rail certificates to union into an ODDFACTOR-YES graph containing a witness of at least `v` edges. Thus any table coordinate whose two rails are both nonzero forces `a>=ceil(v/2)-1`. If no coordinate has both rails, the same fixed low table is present on every YES input, yielding an ODDFACTOR separator of size `a+N-1`; C-291 excludes this below the threshold at `v=(log N)^K`. This establishes `CohEnc>=ceil(v/2)-1`, but that is only polylog N. The useful next target is pair-family diversity and shared-gate reuse. See `research/C293_ODDFACTOR_CERTIFICATE_WIDTH_COHENC_FLOOR_2026-09-28.md`.

Generalization: for any monotone source `f`, writing `W(f)` for minimum positive-certificate width and `L` for cyclic AND complexity gives `CohEnc>=min(ceil(W(f)/2)-1,L-N+1)`. This is a general C-125 tradeoff between polarity variation and direct source recovery, not an ODDFACTOR-specific coincidence. ODDFACTOR realizes `W=v` while C-291 makes `L` much larger than `N+v`.

### Idea 411 - Label odd cuts with high codes and take consensus (C-294)

For ODDFACTOR, each odd cut S|S^c defines a NO completion by taking all bipartite edges internal to either side. Choose a high N-bit code z_[S] for every cut class. Define a source rail to be active when every odd cut compatible with the input gives that coordinate the same bit. These rails are monotone because edge additions remove compatible cuts. A YES graph admits no odd cut, so all rails turn on; a NO graph remains below each compatible high code. This gives a valid semantic C-125 template without an explicit dual-witness sidecar.

For affine labels z_[S](j)=R_j xor |S intersect A_j| mod 2, consensus is exact: if p records odd component sizes and q records the parity of each component's intersection with A_j, the bit is fixed iff q=0 or q=p. But one polarity at each balanced-subset coordinate restricts to ODDFACTOR on a large balanced block, so the cut-consensus circuit inherits superpolynomial AND cost after OR flattening. Scope: this retires only the cut-consensus affine realization. It does not rule out omitting some consensus rails or using nonlinear labels. Next derive whether a cheaper submap can keep YES code coverage without recreating a hard rail. See C-294.

### Idea 412 - Two-code conflict decoding closes the coherent submap escape (C-295)

Take one balanced set A for every output coordinate. Odd-cut labels are either R or complement(R); choose R so both are high. A NO consensus image can only be below one of these two codes or zero. A YES image containing a low table differs from each high code, so OR the rails conflicting with R and OR those conflicting with complement(R), then AND the two results. This one-AND decoder computes ODDFACTOR. Thus every pointwise submap that still covers all YES inputs inherits the superpolynomial monotone AND lower bound. Learning: for a variable NO decoy family, measure the AND complexity of its conflict decoder; simple two-code envelopes merely move the source hardness into the encoder. This does not cover nonlinear labels or maps outside the pointwise-submap order. See C-295.

### Generalization of Idea 412 - Finite high-code envelopes have a conflict decoder (C-295)

If each NO image lies below one of k fixed high tables, form the OR of rails contradicting each table. Every YES image containing a low code conflicts with every high table; each NO image is compatible with at least one. AND the k conflict ORs to compute the source, using k-1 extra AND gates. If the source AND-count is A(f), an encoder with g AND gates must satisfy g >= A(f)-k+1; in particular, k <= A(f)/2 forces g >= A(f)/2. Odd-cut label families can be much larger than the known ODDFACTOR lower bound, so the next question is structured conflict-decoder complexity, not label counting alone.

### Idea 413 - Odd-cut blocker codes are valid, then fixed-code decoding retires them (C-296)

For each coordinate j choose odd-cut family U_j and output its zero rail iff every cut in U_j is crossed by the graph. Every YES graph crosses every odd cut; for NO, a compatible odd component cut T certifies that every active rail agrees with z_T(j)=1[T in U_j]. Random U_j make all labels high, so this is a valid C-125 map. But every YES image contains the fixed zero table, and every NO image excludes it because the high label z_T is nonzero. ANDing the N zero rails computes ODDFACTOR, forcing source-level AND cost. Learning: a large variable NO envelope does not help if the YES low witness is fixed. The next map must vary its low code without exposing a witness-only OR decoder. See C-296.

### Idea 414 - Both sides of a C-125 map must resist envelope decoders (C-297)

A low witness family W covering YES gives the decoder OR_w AND_j F_(j,w_j); a high completion family H covering NO gives AND_z OR_j F_(j,1-z_j). These cost r(N-1) and k-1 additional AND gates, respectively. Thus g>=A(f)-min(k-1,r(N-1)). If either family is small, the map inherits source hardness. The next map must have large low and high envelopes and prevent their shared rail structure from providing a short readout. See C-297.

### Idea 415 - Matching lower-cone test for lifted cut consensus (C-298)

Replace vacuous consensus over an empty set of NO extensions with a monotone lift: a rail is present if some subgraph H has a nonempty compatible odd-cut family unanimous at that bit. NO soundness is automatic because a subgraph has at least as many compatible cuts as its supergraph. On a perfect matching, a rail needs a monochromatic lower cone in the odd matching-boundary poset. This gives an exact test instead of guessing how YES codes vary.

The affine label z_T(j)=c+|T intersect A| mod 2 fails on any matching that has a pair crossing A: toggling the pair preserves the matching boundary but flips the label, so neither rail can be supplied. Every nontrivial A is crossed by some perfect matching. The only affine coordinates surviving every matching are constant across cuts, which make the lift a fixed high code everywhere; a NO-vanishing witness sidecar then exposes ODDFACTOR by OR. This kills the affine lift, not nonlinear labels or general C-125 maps. Next ask whether any nonlinear bit has a monochromatic lower cone for every perfect matching and whether a high N-bit family can be assembled from such bits. See C-298/O-174.

### Idea 416 - Global polarity from alternating-cycle fiber intersections (C-299)

For the C-298 lifted map, each rail on a perfect matching M is present exactly when some singleton-boundary cut fiber F(M,e) is monochromatic. If M and M' form one alternating cycle, every F(M,e) intersects every F(M',f) in an odd cut crossing just e and f. Hence mono-fiber colors agree across neighboring matchings. When v is even and at least 6, relative v-cycles generate the connected matching graph, so every coordinate has one polarity across all perfect matchings. C-125 then forces a fixed low code, whose rail conjunction separates the perfect-matching YES and odd-cut NO distributions; the cited exponential monotone lower bound forces a superpolynomial lift cost.

This resolves the nonlinear label question for the pure lifted-consensus construction. It does not cover separate witness rails W that can fill coordinates on some matching inputs. The key next step is to use matching spread to bound how many inputs W can rescue and then extend polarity through the remaining matching graph. See C-299/O-176.

### Idea 417 - Robust polarity via expander core after spread pruning (C-300; withdrawn)

The proposed proof used Rao's approximation error on its `G(W)` NO distribution to constrain a sidecar assumed to vanish on Cavalar odd-cut NO inputs. Those supports differ, so the inferred sparse exceptional set and the C-300 route-kill do not follow. The alternating-cycle expansion/deletion calculation remains valid only if sparsity is established independently.

Learning: before using a promise-zero condition with a distributional approximation, check that the distributions have matching support or prove a transfer/coupling. Expansion can propagate a property after sparsity is proved; it cannot supply the missing distributional implication. C-301 replaces this attempt with the correct odd-cut approximation.

### Idea 418 - Opposite short terms collide on many odd-cut NO inputs (C-301)

Use Cavalar's matching-DNF approximants, not Rao's `G(W)` approximation. At width `w=floor(v^(1/3)/log v)`, each rail term is a matching of at most w edges. A pair of opposite-polarity terms has union J with at most `2w` edges; J has an isolated vertex, and at least `2^(-2w)` of odd-cut colorings are constant on J's components. Both terms fire there. The shared-DAG over-approximation error is `o(2^(-2w))`, which contradicts one-hot NO soundness if both rails have terms. Therefore every coordinate has one polarity. The YES direction fixes one low table across almost all perfect matchings; its rail conjunction is a distributional ODDFACTOR separator.

At this explicit width, the DNF size is `O(v/log v)=o(v)`, so the DNF agreement lemma applies. It forces the decoder (and hence the map) above `2^floor(v^(1/3)/log v)` size, enough to rule out polynomial-cost maps for `v=(logN)^K`, K>3. Learning: keep the proof inside the approximation theorem's verified parameter range; the published `2^(-omega(w))` shorthand must not be extrapolated to its boundary. This gives no positive decision/reconstruction transfer or P-vs-NP result; the next useful step is a genuinely different source or a sharper comparison to true cyclic decision complexity.

### Idea 419 - Retire raw owner-mask rank; charge selection complexity (C-302)

An individual owner mask is an N-bit vector, so its GF(2) rank is at most N and cannot alone force `q>N^(1+epsilon)`. The parity-lock calibration is sharper: safe canonical hybrids include all even tables, spanning an `(N-1)`-dimensional subspace, while a `4N-4`-rule native cover handles the promise.

Learning: high affine dimension of safe hybrids is not evidence of dangerous recombination. An algebraic measure must capture the grammar's process for selecting compatible masks as the low circuit description varies; raw rank and mask counting erase precisely that coupling. After C-301, the next mechanism is global circuit-description coherence and the independent full-promise near-linear-cover attack. The actual bound remains `q=N-o(N)`.

### Idea 420 - Gap-separator outputs cannot certify circuit nonexistence (C-303)

A native separator is only required to accept `SIZE(s1)` and reject tables outside `SIZE(s2)`. It can also reject a medium table that has a size-`s2` circuit, so a zero evaluation at a high table is not an SoS refutation of `Circuit_s2(z)`. A q-state trace is not a proof certificate unless a separate sound translation is supplied. Austrin--Risse's degree scale is below the current linear q floor for fixed `beta<1`; their size theorem has an extra heuristic-circuit premise. Learning: promise gaps must be totalized before invoking proof systems for exact circuit nonexistence. This route needs both medium-band totalization and a stronger degree parameter; otherwise return effort to O-168's global coherence/full-promise cover problem. No change to q.

### Idea 421 - Native proof support has an exact ideal model but no scalar field valuation (C-304)

Embed consistent supports as monomials `m_S` with conflicting joins set to zero. Upward-closed proof families become monomial ideals; alternative proofs are ideal sums, and compatible joins are ideal products. A complete table is accepted when its full monomial belongs to the output ideal. This realizes the native grammar exactly in dimension `3^N`, but it is not a usual MSP because the target depends on the whole table. Also, idempotence `x+x=x` makes every scalar homomorphism to a field trivial. Learning: any viable span-program bridge must be a compressed subspace/tensor representation rather than a scalar valuation, and raw rank still fails the parity-lock test. No q improvement; keep O-168 primary.

### Idea 422 - Use stationary strategies for global circuit coherence, but account for address memory (C-305)

The native recurrence is an AND-OR reachability game. A positional strategy could encode one circuit wiring choice uniformly across all table addresses, while a universal player challenges an address. The explicit evaluator stores `(gate,address)` and costs `Theta(Ns1)=N^(1+beta-o(1))`. Sharing gate states forgets the address; copying them lets wiring vary by address. Learning: the only plausible near-linear compression is to carry addresses in proof/context supports, where C-281 requires every compatible splice to remain in SIZE(s2). This is a concrete O-168 interface, not a general lower bound; C-257/C-258 remain hostile tests. Actual q unchanged.

### Idea 423 - Context/proof supports cannot enforce address-dependent gate choices (C-306)

For a fixed table w, every context and replacement support matching w is contained in `ell(w)`, so all cross-pairs are compatible. The state recurrence then forgets the support itself and propagates only an active bit. Therefore support labels can record an address but cannot make a shared gate state act on that address; per-address proof choices collapse to `for every x exists d_x`, which accepts arbitrary tables via constant circuits. Learning: retire support tags as control memory. A compact cover must encode one global circuit selector in the state-level activation pattern or use a genuinely different semantic quotient. This is not a lower bound on arbitrary covers; parity/equality remain calibration examples. No q change.
### Idea 424 - Charge the native compiler in AND gates, then test code sources in the right semiring (C-307)

An acyclic monotone separator with a binary AND gates and free OR structure compiles to a native cover with at most a pairs: use each AND gate's two high-side truth carriers as its endpoints. This sharpens the separator-to-cover resource count, but the known native-to-acyclic unrolling still costs q^2, so an acyclic lower bound must exceed N^(2+2epsilon) to force the desired q exponent.

The code-polynomial route needs more care. Standard monotone arithmetic lower bounds rely on every positive cross-product surviving. C-281 multiplication instead sends conflicting partial assignments to zero, which can filter mixed products and synchronize alternatives. Also, bounded-width local-constraint promises have signed monotone CNFs and therefore O(N) native covers when they have O(N) forbidden patterns. Learning: do not select code sources by distance or ordinary arithmetic hardness alone; seek a lower bound for compatible products and show the code is not cheaply locally checkable. No OPS exponent change. See research/C307_COMPATIBLE_CODE_POLYNOMIAL_TRANSFER_AUDIT_2026-09-28.md.


Additional C-307 calibration: expander codes provide 2^(rho N) low objects with linear distance and O(N) bounded-weight parity checks. Their complement promise has an O(N)-pair cover, yet every accepting proof support must be a complete codeword, giving exponentially many full certificates. This shows that neither distance nor certificate abundance charges native states; the hard quantity is the compatible grammar that generates those alternatives. This is not an OPS source because the codewords have not been shown to have circuit size s1.


### Idea 425 - Direct local-clause separators are too large for OPS (C-307)

A CNF separator must have every clause true on every low table. Any falsifying pattern on k<=floor(s1/(4n)) table coordinates extends to a low table by setting all other outputs to zero and hardcoding the at most k one-entries with address minterms. Therefore each non-tautological clause has width >s1/(4n). A random table falsifies one such clause with probability at most 2^(-s1/(4n)); because almost all tables are high, a union bound forces 2^(Omega(s1/n)) clauses, i.e. 2^(Omega(N^beta/log^2N)).

Learning: sparse forbidden-pattern presentations are useful calibrations, but a direct CNF for the OPS gap is already superpolynomial. This does not lower-bound circuits with shared AND subexpressions or cyclic fusion q; the missing mechanism is precisely the compression of exponentially many wide clauses into shared states.

### Idea 426 - Charge matching approximation to AND count, not total gates (C-308)

For a shared monotone DAG with binary AND gates and free arbitrary-fan-in OR gates, assign one matching-DNF approximant per paid AND node. At each AND, flatten its OR-only inputs, form matching unions, pluck, and truncate. The number of distinct width-2w matching terms is bounded by the finite source universe `v^(O(w))`, independent of OR fan-in and circuit-description length; choosing sunflower error `v^(-10w)` makes the per-node D0 error at most `v^(-4w)`. OR roots use exact unions; AND roots reuse their already-counted node approximation, so no output-count factor appears.

Applied to ODDFACTOR C-125 maps, the error is below the `2^(-2w)` odd-cut mass forced by a pair of opposite rail terms. This fixes a common low table on almost every perfect matching; its rail conjunction is a source separator. Reapplying the AND-count approximation to that separator yields `a+N-1>2^w`, with `w=v^(1/3)/(log v)^(2/3+gamma)` and any fixed gamma>0. Learning: gate fan-in normalization was hiding a square-root loss; first ask which logical operations actually need to be paid. The route still gives only a lower bound on encoder cost and no reconstruction/decision separation. See C-308.

### Idea 427 - Distributional decoding only reaches the minimal-witness orbits it sees (C-309)

For a G-invariant monotone function whose minimal YES inputs form one transitive orbit of size L, a sound monotone separator accepting 1-eta of that orbit becomes exact after ORing `floor(log L/log(1/eta))+1` random relabelings. The union bound covers every minimal witness; monotonicity then covers every YES input. This costs only a logarithmic-in-orbit-size factor in the number of circuit copies.

This explains a structural difference between MATCH and ODDFACTOR. Perfect matchings are one orbit and every MATCH-YES input contains one. ODDFACTOR has additional minimal forest witnesses, including paired stars with degree-3 centers, which the perfect-matching distribution never sees. Symmetrizing a decoder from that distribution only gives MATCH, not Odd. Learning: when selecting a source distribution, track minimal YES orbit coverage, not only spread and circuit hardness. A candidate source needs all minimal witness types represented, or a proof that one selected family is upward-cofinal in the YES set. See C-309.

### Idea 428 - Use odd-cut term mass to reach the constant-ratio boundary (C-310)

A width-ell matching term fires on exactly `2^(-ell)` of the odd-cut NO distribution whenever ell<v. Therefore a width-w matching-DNF with D0 acceptance below `2^(-w)` must be empty. In the C-308 shared-DAG approximation, choose `w=c*v^(1/3)/log^(2/3)v` with small constant c so `q=e*r/v<1`; r may now be a small constant fraction of v, rather than o(v). The D0 error remains much smaller than `2^(-w)`, while the D1 tail `q^w` is exponentially small.

This gives every ODDFACTOR C-125 map the bound `a+N-1>16^w` by repeating the canonical-polarity argument and forcing the final separator DNF empty. Learning: when a DNF agreement theorem needs r=o(v), inspect whether the NO distribution gives a lower mass to each short term; direct term mass can bypass that smallness threshold. The bound is now at the `exp(Omega(v^(1/3)/log^(2/3)v))` scale, but no encoder or P-vs-NP transfer has been found. See C-310.

### Idea 429 - Universal dual labels give valid high completions but a one-gate decoder (C-311)

For a span program, let Y_X be the set of dual separators and assign every y an arbitrary high-complexity truth table c(y). The rails `Phi_(j,b)=1 iff every y in Y_X has c(y)[j]=b` are monotone because Y_X shrinks as input edges are added. YES makes Y_X empty, so both rails fire; NO chooses any y in Y_X and gets a high completion. This appears to solve the high-completion problem.

The decisive decoder is `f=Phi_(j,0) AND Phi_(j,1)` for any fixed j: it is true on YES by vacuity and false on NO because a nonempty set of labels cannot be constantly both bits. Thus the map is within one AND gate of exact source decision, regardless of how random or complex the labels are. Learning: high code labels do not create reconstruction savings if the YES profile saturates both polarities. Any surviving algebraic map needs non-vacuous, varying YES completions and must pass the fixed-coordinate pair test first. See `research/C311_UNIVERSAL_DUAL_CONSENSUS_MAP_AND_DECODER_NO_GO_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 430 - A literal-guarded dual map costs at most a factor-two decision compiler (C-312)

Try `Phi_(j,b)=P_(j,b) OR (x_r AND U_(j,b))`, where P are NO-vanishing primal rails carrying low YES codes and U are universal dual-consensus rails. This is a valid monotone C-125 pattern: when x_r=0, NO images are bottom; when x_r=1, NO images use the high dual code; YES uses P.

The two cofactors decode the source. On x_r=0, OR all rails; on x_r=1, AND one fixed opposite-polarity pair. Monotone Shannon decomposition combines the cofactors with at most 2a+2 AND gates if the map costs a. Learning: a literal guard does not give a large reconstruction/decision gap, although the factor-two window is not zero and does not rule out a positive transfer. The primal part for ODDFACTOR still appears as hard as the source. See `research/C312_SINGLE_GUARD_COFACTOR_TRANSFER_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 431 - A one-edge zero slice still contains a hard ODDFACTOR core (C-312)

For any fixed forbidden edge e in K_(v,v), the source cofactor with x_e=0 contains ODDFACTOR_(v-4) as a monotone projection: reserve four vertices on each side including the endpoints of e, place them as leaves in opposite K_(1,3) and K_(3,1) stars that omit e, and isolate this fixed odd-factor forest from the remaining graph. The cofactor is therefore at least `2^((v-4)^Omega(1))` in ordinary monotone AND complexity.

Learning: a literal-guarded dual construction cannot hide the hard computation entirely in the dual-active branch; its zero-decoy/primal branch already contains essentially the same superpolynomial source. This still does not compare the encoder to the full cyclic source with an additive margin. See C-312 and C-291.

### Idea 432 - A semantic guard does not inherit literal Shannon decoding (C-313)

C-312 works because the guard is a source literal and gives exact decoders on both literal cofactors. For a general monotone guard `g`, decoding the guard-zero region requires selecting with `not g`; monotone composition cannot do that automatically. In the universal-dual pattern, aggregate signals `D=OR(all rails)`, one pair `R`, and `g` may take `(1,0,0)` on a YES input and `(1,0,1)` on a NO input. Since the YES vector is coordinatewise below the NO vector, no monotone decoder using only those aggregates can distinguish them.

This does not rule out a full-rail decoder or a bounded literal-cofactor family. It rules out treating a one-bit semantic guard as if it were a Shannon variable. Next work must charge the guard's false-positive NO profiles or recover a global selector from the full rail vector. See `research/C313_ARBITRARY_GUARD_IS_NOT_A_LITERAL_COFACTOR_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 433 - Cover the prefix-block safe envelope (C-314)

Partition truth-table inputs into k=Theta(log N) prefix blocks. Every size-s1 table restricts to a size-s1 circuit on each block. Conversely, independent block circuits of size s1 synthesize to a whole table of size k*s1+O(k loglogN)<=s2. This gives a safe superset `A_k(s1)` containing all low tables, and every high table has at least one block restriction of size above s1.

The obstacle is locating such a block inside the native closure without a free circuit-complexity oracle. Explicit block/gate/address evaluation still costs Theta(N*s1); support tags have already failed as address registers in C-306. This is an interface for a global selector argument, not a cover or lower bound. Preserve the C-257/C-258/C-281 checks. See C-314.

### Idea 434 - Turn prefix blocks into a local constant-gap/direct-sum problem (C-315)

For k=Theta(log N) blocks, a blockwise separator for `SIZE(s1)` versus block complexity above `s2/k` combines by AND: all restrictions of a global low table pass, and a global high table must have one block above `s2/k`. The local gap is only a constant factor, and copying the local circuit k times yields the straightforward upper bound. This isolates what a near-linear construction would need to compress: a shared selector for the blockwise local gap.

Counting shows this regime is real, not just a formal reduction. There are globally high tables with every block restriction between `B*s1` and `A*s1` for fixed constants: use a Lupanov-sized family of arbitrary functions on a fixed small address subcube in each block, remove functions of complexity at most `B*s1`, and compare product-family cardinality against all global size-`s2` circuits. Learning: the safe envelope cannot be strengthened to say a high table has a block with a growing complexity ratio over s1. A viable route must exploit exact `>s1` block detection and cross-block sharing. No q lower bound follows. See `research/C315_PREFIX_BLOCK_CONSTANT_GAP_AND_DISTRIBUTED_HARDNESS_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 435 - Exact algebraic fingerprints collapse to address evaluation (C-316)

Model the entire truth table as the pointwise algebra `F_2^N`. Its N address indicators are pairwise orthogonal idempotents. If unital algebra homomorphisms collectively detect every table difference, their product is injective and their total target dimension is at least N; a field-valued homomorphism selects exactly one address. A linear sketch used to test equality with some low witness also needs rank `N-O(s2 log(s2+n))`, since its kernel must contain only size-s2 tables and the zero table is low.

The explicit gate-by-address evaluation cost is `O(N*s1)`, outside the `N^(1+o(1))` target. Learning: exact algebraic fingerprints and linear equality sketches do not compress the address dimension. This is a scoped route filter only; it says nothing about nonlinear promise-specific summaries or general fusion covers. Do not revisit without an interface that avoids exact difference detection and the equality-sketch form. See `research/C316_ALGEBRAIC_FINGERPRINT_ROUTE_FILTER_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 436 - Separate independent block entropy from global circuit coherence (C-317)

For `k=Theta(log N)` prefix blocks, a product family of locally moderate-hard functions is globally high with overwhelming probability once its cardinality beats `|SIZE(s2)|` by an exponential margin. But a product safe cylinder of dimension `Theta(s2 log s2)` can vary independently in every block and still have all completions in `SIZE(s2)`, while repeated identical blocks share one small global circuit. Therefore neither local hardness nor the number of blockwise owner switches measures the separator's cost. The missing object is the global circuit-description correlation among the restrictions. A useful invariant must charge how the native grammar excludes independent tuples while permitting compatible shared-description tuples; count-free coordinates only up to the `Theta(s2 log s2)` ceiling. This is a calibration and next-question refinement, not a q lower bound. See `research/C317_BLOCKWISE_SAFE_CYLINDER_TENSORIZATION_2026-09-28.md`.

### Idea 437 - Treat block restrictions as a shared cofactor ensemble (C-318)

For a global function `f(a,y)`, its k prefix restrictions form `F(y)=(f_a(y))_a`. In a k-lane circuit whose AND/OR/NOT gates act coordinatewise, suffix inputs are diagonal and prefix inputs are fixed masks. Scalar circuits lift to this cofactor vector gate-for-gate; vector wires scalarize by selecting the lane indexed by the scalar prefix. Therefore global circuit size equals this structured ensemble-circuit size. The native grammar has its own lane-wide operation on support vectors, with conflict filtering. Direct-sum is consequently a comparison of two SIMD algebras, not a sum of k unrelated local costs. Seek a bridge/lower bound for the compatible-support SIMD grammar and preserve C-257/C-258; this is a model reformulation, not a q lower bound. See `research/C318_COFACTOR_ENSEMBLE_AND_NATIVE_SIMD_MODEL_2026-09-28.md`.

In promise terms, every proof support is a product box over block lanes; low ensembles must be covered by generated boxes and every box must stay inside the high circuit-size ceiling. This gives the exact compatible-box interpolation problem. The box language remains globally coupled through arbitrary endpoints, so a tensor theorem still needs a transfer argument.

### Idea 438 — Analyze the native system as an alternating state graph (C-319)

Each fusion state i obeys the exact two-obligation recurrence `x_i=(A_i OR predecessors_E) AND (B_i OR predecessors_H)`, where each seed is a consistent signed-literal disjunction and predecessor edges are fixed by endpoint containment. The least fixed point is an input-labelled alternating reachability game; one state can query literals in every cofactor lane. This identifies the object a direct-sum theorem must handle and explains why lanewise circuit additivity is not automatic.

Two natural state surrogates fail before reaching q: the minimum safe-box cover of `SIZE(s1)` has a singleton cover of size `|SIZE(s1)|`, so its log is only `N^(beta+o(1))`; and the acceptance indicator has rank at most `|SIZE(s2)|`, whose log is also sublinear. Free-coordinate entropy is capped separately by C-317. The surviving target is a q-sensitive synchronization invariant of the transition graph and signed seed clauses that distinguishes independent cofactor descriptions from shared ones, while passing the C-257 parity and C-258 equality covers. This is a route refinement, not a lower bound. See `research/C319_NATIVE_CLOSURE_AS_ALTERNATING_COFACTOR_GAME_2026-09-28.md`.
